hello.note: Both syllables dip, so 'nee' comes out rising.

slang.note: Loanword; fine for friends/peers, too breezy for elders.
Casual, near-universal now; less fitting at formal partings.

how_are_you.note: Understood everywhere, though a little textbook.

slang.note: Casual check-in for someone you know; not for elders.

thank_you.note: First falls sharply, second is light and quick.

youre_welcome.note: Reply to thanks; after an apology, may gwahn-shee.

slang.note: Adds 'my pleasure' warmth; fine with friends, staff, strangers.

no_problem.note: Casual 'it's nothing'; also softens an apology.

slang.note: Northern/Beijing casual, erhua'd; close friends and family.

please.note: Prefixes a request: cheeng gay wor, 'please give me'.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'may I ask'; to squeeze past, jyeh-gwor.

yes.note: No plain 'yes' in Mandarin; this is 'that's right'.

no.note: 'boo' turns rising here; 'shr' is a buzz, no vowel.

of_course.note: Emphatic yes; 'dahng' stays high and level, 'rahn' rises.

slang.note: Playful, upbeat 'of course!'; friends and banter, not formal.

amazing.note: 'tai' rhymes with 'eye', like dzai in goodbye.

slang.note: Playful praise among friends; too casual for elders.

delicious.note: hun-how dip, hun rises; chr buzzes like shr; how-huh for drinks.

cheers.note: Literally 'dry the cup'; both syllables high, flat.

slang.note: Casual toast at dinners/bars; less formal than gahn-bay.
